extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for reviewers of submissions to ICLR 2022, covering reading, writing, discussion, ethics, conflicts, and recommendation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and substance of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a constructive, thorough and timely review during the review period (dates provided). Engage in discussion and provide a final recommendation by the deadline. Be responsive in the discussion phase (able to respond within 3 business days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: You must adhere to our Code of Ethics in your role as a reviewer. You must also adhere to our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the CoE report for assigned papers and flag any potential CoE violations. If uncertain, reach out to your area chair. For other violations (plagiarism, double submission, formatting, etc.), contact the AC or PC as appropriate, e.g., via an official comment with readership restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and maintain OpenReview/DBLP profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Create your OpenReview profile and link your DBLP profile (by September 15th 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping profile information up-to-date helps conflict-of-interest detection and assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Bid on papers during the bidding window (7 October 2021 - 12 October 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bids to indicate interest and conflicts (see conflict guidance below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid being assigned papers that present a conflict of interest and flag conflicts when found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update OpenReview profile (co-authors, past/current institutions) to help automated detection. If you find a conflict while bidding, bid 'Very Low'. If assigned a conflicted paper, contact the program chairs immediately to have it re-assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the entire paper and related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read through the entire paper, and look up related work and citations to comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time. Consider supplementary material when it may answer questions that arise while reading the main paper (it's not necessary but often helpful).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine the paper's objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider what the goal of the paper is (address known problem, introduce new application/problem, theoretical finding, or combination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations as to potential value and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess strong points
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the submission is clear, technically correct, experimentally rigorous, reproducible, and whether it presents novel findings (theoretically, algorithmically, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List strong points in the review; be positive and generous in summarizing contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess weak points
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify weaknesses in clarity, correctness, experiments, reproducibility, novelty, or other aspects listed under strong points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive in listing weak points; these can guide author revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of bias and community value
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open-minded about the value and interest a paper can hold for the entire ICLR community, even if it may not be interesting to you personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't reject a paper just because you don't find it 'interesting' — lack of immediate interest is not a valid criterion for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer three key evaluation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: When forming a recommendation, answer: (1) What is the specific question/problem tackled? (2) Is the approach well motivated and placed in the literature? (3) Does the paper support the claims (are results correct and scientifically rigorous)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these as the core of your decision to accept or reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize your review by summarizing claims, listing strong and weak points, clearly stating recommendation with key reasons, providing supporting arguments, asking clarifying questions, and giving additional feedback to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the review easy to navigate and useful to authors and area chairs. Explicitly state where you're uncertain and what you'd like clarified in rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness and constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite in your review; ask whether you'd be happy to receive the review you wrote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide feedback framed as helpful suggestions rather than hostile criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and concreteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be precise and concrete in your comments; include references to back up any claims, especially about novelty and prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant literature when asserting missing comparisons or prior-art issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is not necessary to read but may answer questions; consider it before asking authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant questions can be resolved by the supplement, consult it prior to requesting additional experiments or clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may ask for additional experiments, but justify why they are necessary to push the paper over the acceptance threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New experiments should not significantly change the submission's content; they should be limited in scope and serve to validate existing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission does not achieve state-of-the-art results, that alone is not grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers can provide new, relevant, impactful, or insightful knowledge without being SOTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for citing recent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not required to compare to contemporaneous papers published within the last four months before the deadline; reviewers should use judgment about citing very recent work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers published in peer-reviewed proceedings within four months prior to the deadline may be considered contemporaneous. ArXiv-only works are not required to be known by authors; if in doubt discuss with AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling policy violations and ethics issues
rubrics_metrics.description: To flag a CoE violation, indicate it in the CoE report for that paper; AC will work with PC and ethics board. For other violations (plagiarism, double submission, etc.), contact AC or PC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can file an official comment with appropriate readership restrictions to notify chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact Area Chair
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the AC via the paper's OpenReview page by adding an official comment and adding ACs to the list of 'Readers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OpenReview official comments for formal communication with ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in and be responsive during discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in asynchronous discussion with authors, other reviewers, and ACs to clarify and improve the paper during the discussion phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be able to respond to comments/requests within 3 business days and update your review taking into account the discussion and any author revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a final recommendation considering new information
rubrics_metrics.description: Update your review and provide a final recommendation to the area chair by the deadline, considering discussion and revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain openness to changing your initial recommendation either more positive or more negative in light of new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical review-writing examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow example structures (as shown in accept/reject examples): a clear summary, enumerated pros and cons, concrete questions for rebuttal, typos/minor comments, and post-rebuttal updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples as templates: be structured, precise, include suggested ablations/experiments when relevant, and list specific minor corrections.
